rv.q: In a world where everything seems to be a fight more than ever before, this tight and taut one-hour show is beautifully choreographed, energetically performed and held my attention from start to finish.
It’s moments like these when Chloe divulges that her tough exterior masks a joyously matter-of-fact romanticism, rendering her a thoroughly sympathetic character.
Despite that slight caveat, this is a superb revival.
Campbell's performance alone justifies the ticket price and the journey to Dalston; a feat of endurance, charisma and emotional transparency that marks her as a genuinely exciting stage talent.
This is a jam-packed sixty minutes that grabs your attention from the first word to the final lighting cue.

cn.t: Critics praise this emotionally charged solo show for its sharp writing and demanding performance, with Campbell delivering the physical and emotional commitment required to land Josephine's punchy exploration of grief, ambition, and love.
